text:
cheng: Heads-up — saw a regression on Private VPC smallgpu pools after the continuous-batching tweak. p95 jumped from ~220ms -> ~420ms on tail workloads (many short chats).

maria: ugh. which knobs did you flip? slab allocator change?

cheng: rolled kernel selection heuristic + enabled slab batch coalescing (default max_batch_size 128 -> 160 for smallgpu slice). Also turned on token_budget_target auto for throughput.

ajay: profiler shows a small-batch starvation effect. Large coalesced batches (128-160) are building up and holding the queue while tiny requests wait. memcpy spikes when falling back to the slow kernel.

tim: can you paste the perf numbers and a quick trace?

cheng: p50 stable, p95/99 up. sample trace: 
```
request A (2 tokens) enqueued -> waits 80ms while batch 120 forms -> large kernel chosen -> kernel fallback (slow memcpy) adds 60ms -> finish
request B (30 tokens) waits -> completes in batch
```

maria: so two problems: batch-formation policy and kernel selection thresholds for avg_seq_len. For private constrained hardware we should bias toward smaller max_batch_size and lower token_budget_target.

ajay: agreed. proposal: 
- smallgpu pool overrides: max_batch_size: 48
- token_budget_target: 250 (was 800)
- queue_priority: give small requests preemptive weight (preemptive_pct: 20)
- kernel_choice: prefer small-token kernels if batch_mean_seq <= 64
- kv_cache_ejection_threshold: 0.7 (eject cold entries earlier)

maria: +1. Also add an early-serve path: if a head-of-queue request waiting > 50ms and batch size < 8, serve it solo (bypass coalesce). That avoids pathological tail.

tim: how do we push this to Private? Customers are still on the default runtime.yaml in their VPC images. We need a config override mechanism per cluster.

ajay: we already support per-cluster override in /etc/redwood/overrides.yaml. sample override snippet that ops can apply in customer VPC: 
```
# /etc/redwood/overrides.yaml
runtime:
  batching:
    smallgpu:
      max_batch_size: 48
      token_budget_target: 250
      preemptive_pct: 20
      early_serve_ms: 50
  kernel_selection:
    prefer_small_token_threshold: 64
  kv_cache:
    ejection_threshold: 0.7
```

maria: can you run A/B in a canary slice and gather p50/p95/p99 + kernel-switch counts + memcpy time? aim for 1% of capacity first.

cheng: starting canary now on 1 node (slice-c) with override applied. will post numbers in ~15m.

sre-bot: Deploy started: canary slice-c override apply by changelist #4567. ETA ~8m.

ajay: also instrument a new metric: batch_wait_time_by_size to see how long small requests sit behind large batches. add to console charts.

maria: if this canary proves out, let's make a smallgpu default profile for Private customers (opt-in) and document tradeoffs. I'll write a short runbook for support.

cheng: can confirm after 18m — first pass looks promising: p95 down to ~240ms on canary, memcpy stdev reduced. sharing logs in a sec. :thumbsup:

maria: awesome. once we stabilize, we should backport the small-token kernel preference into the main heuristic so Hosted doesn't regress when load mixes change.

tim: agreed. action items: 
- ajay: add metric & tighten kernel threshold (PR)
- maria: runbook + support note
- cheng: expand canary to 10% and monitor
- tim: coordinate override rollout for affected customers

cheng: assigning owners and will keep thread updated. thanks all.
